message: Agent registration completed successfully with admin approval polling. Tokens saved automatically.
Authentication verified; token valid with 1-hour TTL. CLI manages token lifecycle automatically post-registration.
API catalog browsed successfully via `jentic apis list`. Single test API discovered with 1 operation.
Agent initially attempted `jentic api` (incorrect) before correcting to `jentic apis`. Help text suggested correct command but created minor UX friction.
Test API located via `jentic apis show`. Full reference format (vendor/name/version) required; authentication requirement (X-API-Key header) inferred from setup notes rather than spec.
OpenAPI spec did not explicitly document X-API-Key authentication requirement. Users may struggle with implicit auth types without external documentation.
Operations endpoint queried successfully. Single operation identified: `GET /get` (Simple GET endpoint).
OpenAPI specification downloaded and examined via `jentic apis spec` command.
Access request filed and approved for jentic-test/test-api toolkit. System auto-approved in test environment after human-gated approval flow.
Agent discovered access flow through error messages rather than proactive toolkit discovery. No `jentic toolkits list` command available; users must learn requirements reactively.
Proxied GET request executed successfully through Jentic broker. Response returned 200 status with expected body. Execution record created with metadata (execution ID, toolkit ID, upstream status).
Broker automatically injected authentication credentials; no manual header management required. Seamless credential abstraction from agent perspective.
